edit.description: the listing leg decides on the row's type and hands its object id to the content leg; the row decode shared with `listTreeBlobNames` beside it
the non-blob arm, and the one-tree pin moved from the folded sha to the object id

summary: `readFileAtRef` hands back `git show <ref>:<dir>`'s tree listing as a file's committed bytes; its own contract is bytes-or-absent and a non-blob row has no verdict
acceptance: `readFileAtRef` answers a blob's committed bytes or `null`, and nothing else. Its listing leg reads the row's type and object id — the `ls-tree -z` row decode `listTreeBlobNames` beside it already performs, shared rather than spelled twice (`.claude/rules/engineering.md`, *The fix lands at the mechanism*) — a non-blob row answers the `null` the reader already gives a path that is not in the tree, and the content leg reads that object id. No `rev-parse` leg and no `<ref>:<path>` composition left: an object id cannot move, so the one-tree property the fold buys today is structural instead. The existing one-sha pin moves to the object id rather than being dropped, and the doc's `git show <ref>:<path>` narration states what the legs now are. `pnpm tsc --noEmit`, the suite, and the export and citation pins green.
tests: a directory committed at the ref reads back absent, never git's own tree listing as content
the content leg reads the object id the listing named, never a `<ref>:<path>` composition
notes: Verified on disk and against git 2.43 this tick. `src/git.ts:722`-`:739` probes presence with `ls-tree --name-only`, then `show <sha>:<path>`; over a committed directory git prints `tree <sha>:<dir>` plus the child names, which the reader returns as content though its doc (`:670`) says bytes-or-`null`. Reached through `harness/citeResolver.ts`'s `per` reads, so a cite at a directory refuses on the section — the wrong half blamed. The non-blob verdict is the price f66ad0f5 named.
